Google, Mesa, AZ.water_source: The facility is air-cooled for its technical operations; water use is minimal and confined to office/sanitary purposes. [27]

Since a portion of the city's water supply is from the Colorado River, this represents a significant reduction in the potential draw from that system.

Digital Realty, Chandler, AZ.water_source: Estimated from a reported use of 0.7 million gallons per day at full load. [2]

Microsoft, Goodyear & El Mirage, AZ.water_source: An analysis Microsoft shared with the Goodyear city council estimated the data center's water use. [5, 7] The water is supplied by the City of Goodyear, whose portfolio includes groundwater and Colorado River water delivered by the Central Arizona Project. [5]
Microsoft, Goodyear & El Mirage, AZ.cooling_type: Adiabatic/direct evaporative cooling, which uses outside air when temperatures are below 85°F and water for evaporative cooling above that temperature. [4, 12, 15]
Microsoft, Goodyear & El Mirage, AZ.planned_buildout_note: The surrounding land is actively being developed. Microsoft is expanding its campus on adjacent, recently acquired land, and other hyperscale data center operators like QTS and Vantage are also building in the immediate vicinity. [6, 17, 25]
Microsoft, Goodyear & El Mirage, AZ.savings_note: Microsoft has stated that its future data centers in the area will use air-cooled systems and is piloting a 'Zero Water Initiative' design that could save approximately 42 million gallons per facility annually. [3, 5]

Meta, Mesa, AZ.water_source: Estimated based on 450 MW IT load at 85% load factor and Meta's reported fleet-average Water Usage Effectiveness (WUE) of 0.24 L/kWh. [15] The City of Mesa's water supply includes Colorado River water from the Central Arizona Project. [16]
Meta, Mesa, AZ.cooling_type: Advanced evaporative/indirect cooling; Meta has deployed StatePoint Liquid Cooling (SPLC) in hot climates, which uses air to cool water. [15]
Meta, Mesa, AZ.planned_buildout_note: The data center is an anchor of Mesa's Elliot Road Technology Corridor, which was planned by the city to attract tech investment. The surrounding land is actively being developed with other major tech companies like Google and Apple, as well as industrial, commercial, and retail projects. [12, 7, 22]
Meta, Mesa, AZ.savings_note: The maximum saveable water is the site's entire estimated annual process water consumption. This could be achieved by converting the campus from its current water-efficient evaporative cooling system to a 100% closed-loop, dry cooling system, which would eliminate water loss from evaporation, leaving only minimal consumption for office and humidification needs. Meta's newest designs for AI data centers utilize such closed-loop systems. [8]

CyrusOne, Chandler, AZ.water_source: Circle of Blue, 'Data Centers a Small, But Growing Factor in Arizona’s Water Budget', https://www.circleofblue.org/2024/world/data-centers-a-small-but-growing-factor-in-arizonas-water-budget/ [13]

This minimal amount, used for essential humidification and domestic purposes, represents the maximum that could be offset. CyrusOne already runs a 'net-positive water' program to restore more water to local watersheds than it consumes. [17]
